Customer to share sample prompt sets and p95 targets spreadsheet
Schedule follow-up technical deep dive with infra team week of Feb 9

header:
Date: 2026-01-29T15:00:00Z
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Marta Lopez (Sandstone CTO), Jamal Patel (Sandstone Infra), Simone Rios (Sandstone Product)
summary: Discovery focused on p95 latency targets and burst throughput. Sandstone wants hosted for dev, with Dedicated or Private for production due to data residency and audit. Discussed streaming vs non-streaming token rates, concurrency needs, and fallback strategies. Agreed Redwood will run a 3-day hosted spike test and follow up with deeper infra session.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we're on for 56 minutes, I think. Quick intros?
[00:08] Marta Lopez (Sandstone CTO): Hi, Marta here. CTO. We've got Jamal and Simone with me.
[00:12] Jamal Patel (Sandstone Infra): Jamal, infra. Hi.
[00:15] Simone Rios (Product): Simone, product.
[00:18] Alex Chen: Great. Priya, want to say hi?
[00:20] Priya Raman (Redwood SE): Hey, Priya, SE on infra and perf. I'll lead the profiling part after we do a quick qual.
[00:25] Alex Chen: Cool. Goal for today: understand your p95 targets, concurrency, streaming needs, and whether hosted/dedicated/private fits. Also agree next steps. Sound good?
[00:34] Marta: Yep. We're evaluating because our user-facing assistant is moving to real-time summaries, and p95 matters — can't be more than 400ms for short responses.
[00:42] Jamal: Also want to plan for bursts — Black Friday type spikes but for our retail clients, so token/sec can jump 10x for minutes.
[00:49] Alex Chen: OK. When you say 400ms p95, is that for the whole API call or server-side token generation time?
[00:55] Simone: Whole end-to-end from client to final token, inc network, but we can separate. We really care about perceived latency to users.
[01:03] Priya: Understood. Quick stack check — currently hosted on GCP, using internal model endpoints on GPU instances, right? Any KV cache or prefix caching?
[01:12] Jamal: Yes, GCP. We're using a mix of internal endpoints and a few open models. No shared KV cache today, every request hits the model.
[01:19] Alex Chen: That matters for cost and latency — caching can shave significant ms for repeated prompts.
[01:24] Marta: We considered adding caching but worried about PII and retention.
[01:27] Priya: We can do ephemeral prefix caching and TTLs with encryption, or use Redwood's KV approach — forgive my pronunciation, sometimes our transcript says KV cash —
[01:36] Jamal: (laughs) KV cash, yes.
[01:39] Alex Chen: Let's dig into traffic shape. What's typical RPS and peak concurrent conversations?
[01:44] Jamal: Steady-state 18 RPS across the region, peaks up to 320 RPS during campaigns. Conversation length averages 120 tokens, but summaries push 400–600 tokens per user in some flows.
[01:55] Priya: So bursts are both higher RPS and longer token generations — that lattice is the worst case for p95. For streaming do you need partial token streaming to clients?
[02:04] Simone: Yes, product requires progressive streaming for UX — as tokens arrive we render them. p95 should still be under 400ms to first token for short prompts.
[02:12] Alex Chen: Got it. For hosted vs dedicated vs private — quick run-through: hosted gives fastest time-to-test, Dedicated buys you predictable throughput and isolation, Private gives VPC/on-prem with KMS for audit. Do you have data residency or SOC 2 constraints?
[02:24] Marta: Need SOC 2 and audit logs for enterprise customers. Data residency for EU clients maybe. Also our security team wants key control — so KMS/HSM is desirable.
[02:33] Jamal: Yep and SSO with SAML.
[02:35] Priya: Redwood Private supports a private control plane and customer-managed networking; we can show audit log flow. But to validate latency and burst behavior, a hosted pilot is faster.
[02:44] Marta: We're open to a hosted pilot provided tokens don't leave EU region, is that possible?
[02:49] Alex Chen: Yes, we can provision hosted endpoints in europe-region and limit egress. We'll include region pinning in the pilot.
[02:56] Jamal: One key question — how do you guarantee p95 under burst? We need to understand batching and queuing behavior.
[03:02] Priya: Good question. Redwood's runtime does continuous batching with workload-aware heuristics, and there's an autoscaler for Dedicated. For hosted, we can provision burst capacity but SLAs differ. We talked about fallback policies — if a big spike hits, requests can be routed to cheaper model variants or to Dedicated pools.
[03:17] Simone: Can you do canary rollouts if we pin model versions? We want to avoid regressions in quality when switching quantized models.
[03:24] Priya: Yes, model pinning and canary rollouts with traffic split are supported; Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles per workload.
[03:30] Alex Chen: Marta, do you have a target concurrency per user or per tenant?
[03:33] Marta: Per tenant concurrency roughly 75 concurrent open dialogs; per-user concurrency small. But some enterprise tenants can spawn many parallel sessions, so planning for tenant-level concurrency important.
[03:44] Jamal: Also need the p95 for streaming throughput — tokens/sec per GPU. What's realistic?
[03:49] Priya: Depends on model and quantization. For a 7B open model on A100-ish hardware we typically hit 350–600 tokens/sec in single-stream configurations; quantization and kernel selection can push that higher. For 70B models it's much lower. But continuous batching can improve aggregate tokens/sec at the expense of first-token latency if you increase batch windows.
[04:08] Alex Chen: Do you have a list of models you plan to use?
[04:11] Jamal: We're testing a custom-finetuned 13B and sometimes use a Llama 2-70B fallback.
[04:17] Priya: That clarifies costs and p95. 13B is a good middle ground. For 13B we can hit first-token in sub-200ms on Dedicated with optimized kernels if sequence length small. But with 500–600 token outputs and streaming, tail latency depends on KV cache reuse.
[04:33] Simone: We're worried about cold-starts during holidays. How quickly can Dedicated spin up more capacity?
[04:38] Priya: Dedicated has configurable autoscale policies with warm pools and burst capacity; if you want strict p95 guarantees in production, Dedicated with warm pool is recommended. Hosted can also be configured but less predictable.
[04:49] Alex Chen: Let's talk specific test. We propose a 3-day hosted spike test: we host compatible model in EU region, run your sample prompt set with simulated traffic (benched to match your RPS and spikes), capture p95, token/sec, and streaming first-token latencies. Does that work?
[05:03] Marta: Yes, but we need the exact profiling plan and what artifacts you'll share.
[05:07] Priya: We'll provide a bench harness, detailed dashboard access with token-level breakdowns, trace hooks, and a reporting sheet. We'll also include failure modes and fallback logs.
[05:18] Jamal: Ok. One more: encryption and KMS — can Redwood route logs to our SIEM and keep audit logs for 1 year?
[05:25] Alex Chen: Yes for Dedicated and Private we can integrate with your SIEM and set longer retention for audit logs. Hosted has retention limits but we can discuss an add-on.
[05:33] Simone: What's the expected cost delta between hosted pilot and Dedicated steady-state for our estimated RPS?
[05:39] Priya: We'll provide an estimated cost model: per-token for hosted during pilot, then a Dedicated commit estimate with baseline GPU pools. We'll include cost per token and cost per p95 improvement scenarios.
[05:50] Marta: The security team will ask about SOC 2, ISO, SAML SSO. Can you send certs?
[05:56] Alex Chen: Yes, I'll send the security pack and SOC 2 report.
[06:00] Jamal: For the bench harness, we need to emulate streaming clients — partial frames and early cancellations.
[06:06] Priya: We'll include those scenarios. Also simulate token truncation and network jitter.
[06:11] Alex Chen: Quick note, Simone — you mentioned progressive rendering; we'll measure time-to-first-token and time-to-50%-completion as part of the report.
[06:19] Simone: Perfect.
[06:21] Marta: Any blockers from Redwood side?
[06:24] Alex Chen: None on our side. We'll need your sample prompt set, model artifacts if using custom weights (or at least a close proxy), and a contact for infra to coordinate region pinning.
[06:35] Jamal: I'll share a S3 bucket with prompts and a small subset of model traces.
[06:40] Alex Chen: Great. Recap: Redwood to run 3-day hosted spike test in EU region, include bench harness, dashboards, and a report. Redwood to send pricing/pilot terms and security pack. Sandstone to share prompt set, sample traces, and identify infra contact. Follow-up deep dive week of Feb 9.
[06:58] Marta: Sounds good.
[07:02] Alex Chen: Any final questions?
[07:05] Simone: Just one — in failure modes, if Dedicated pool saturated, can requests be routed to a lower-cost hosted model with graceful degradation?
[07:13] Priya: Yes, routing policies support fallbacks to compatible model variants and region failover. We can show sample policy configs.
[07:21] Jamal: Good.
[07:23] Alex Chen: Alright we'll follow up with the items. Thanks everyone.
[07:26] Marta: Thanks.
[07:28] (call ends)

Notes on transcript accuracy: occasional mis-identified product names (e.g., Redwood Dedicate vs Dedicated), "KV cash" transcriptions, and punctuation inconsistencies.
